title: The Case of the $5 Chocolate Bar
your_side: My client picked up a chocolate bar, got distracted by a phone call, and walked out still holding it without realising she hadn't paid. She returned to the store to pay as soon as she noticed. There was no intent to steal. The store clerk says she walked past the till and out the door with an unpaid item, and that the exit is well past the registers, so the Crown will argue that leaving with unpaid goods shows intent to take them. The defence's position is that theft requires the intent to deprive the owner of the item, and that an honest, distracted mistake — promptly corrected by returning to pay — is not theft.
